what_failed: Grew a lot, then post-pandemic transport costs rose and work fell drastically; recovery began in 2022
Peak months (April-June) mean very high volume and overtime
numbers: Sales/workload doubled in 2023 (self-reported)
25 employees in the sewing workshop
Hotels replace linen once every 2-3 years, partly because poor laundries' detergents ruin it
2024 summer orders started in January
Planned laundry: 12 tonnes per 8-hour shift; considering daily linen rental to small and medium hotels

business: Zor Technology
product: imported consumer electronics (USB drives, MP3 players) from Chinese suppliers
timeline: Started at 16 on eBay, moved to own website; shut down less than 12 months later after a law firm's call
what_worked: No paid marketing: sales through word of mouth and referrals
Friends sold with flyers as informal affiliates ($15 per $55 sale)
what_failed: An MP3 player too similar to a major brand's product: told to stop trading immediately or be sued; could not ship pending orders or keep the name
eBay as the first channel was a poor long-term solution
numbers: $1,000 start
MP3 player bought at $4.20, sold at $49.95
'On track to do 6 figures' in year 1 (self-reported)

business: CROSSNET
product: four-way volleyball net (own product, contract manufacturer)
start_capital: 'very little money in the bank' (amount not stated)
timeline: About a year of sample rounds with the manufacturer over WhatsApp while working full time; first 100 nets, then 200, later 7,500-unit orders
what_worked: Started small: bought 100 nets, sold them, re-bought 200; avoided debt
Influencer product exchanges, starting small with people they could contact directly
what_failed: Worst mistake: took orders before the final product and enough stock were in the warehouse; 'a few weeks turned into a few months'
Did not break down and negotiate every cost from day one; would have been profitable sooner
numbers: First order 100 units, second 200, later 7,500-unit increments
Target $5,000,000 sales in 2020 (self-reported)

business: Florjan-V (towel maker, Albania)

start_capital: not stated; grew with USAID-backed loans
timeline: Doubled in size over eight years (USAID story last updated March 2006)
what_worked: Product with steady everyday consumption ('you'll use a towel at least six times a day')
Paid off a first loan to repair equipment, which helped double production; a second loan bought a generator and a minivan to deliver towels to retailers and wholesalers
Added own brand labels and new patterns and designs on donor advice

Described as the only towel maker in Albania; growing presence in Kosovo and Montenegro

business: Market evidence: Horecatex (Romania) advertorial

Sells on stock and speed: 1,000 m2 warehouse, over 150 pallets always in stock, delivery within 24-48 hours anywhere in Romania (company claim)
Oeko-Tex certified towels and linen

numbers: 1,000 m2 warehouse, 150+ pallets in stock, 24-48 h delivery (claims)

business: Branded-goods boutique turned online-only shop (Tirana)

Market players say about 30% of online clothing orders are returned by buyers

business: Small grocery shop, Vushtrri

business: Small neighbourhood shop, Ulpiana (Prishtina)

Cannot afford to stock pricier lines (e.g. meat) because nobody buys them there
numbers: Income halved by supermarkets (owner's estimate)

business: AlbPastrim sh.p.k. (cleaning services, staff training and cleaning products)

Small rivals undercut on price for households

business: Buyer evidence: three-apartment daily-rental host, Tirana (outside the Ring road)

what_failed: Oversupply: nightly price fell to 40 euros (2023) and 30 euros (2024) in her area
High energy costs (guests kept air conditioning on), equipment wore out fast, 'sheets and towels had to be bought often'
Euro fall: same flat earned about 40% less in lekë in 2024 than 2022
numbers: 60 euros/night 2022 -> 30-40 euros/night 2024
Now long-term at 500-600 euros a month
note: Host (buyer) quit daily rentals: the plan's customer, not a seller. Same article quotes PikHost (Brendi Hoti): more properties, fewer bookings each, managers cut prices; only high-quality and luxury properties unaffected

Net 100-400 euros/month

Steadier demand from foreigners staying days or weeks for work

Finding under-priced items in unsorted thrift shops

Items bought for about 3-4 euros resold for about 10

business: Aleksandër Asimi flower shop and importer (Tirana)

business: Mali proizvođači online shop (Belgrade)
product: food from small Serbian farm producers, bought in and delivered weekly in Belgrade

Free-delivery campaign brought turnover and new customers
Adding eggs, cured meats and cheese pleased customers; in August turnover equalled the first six months

Did not budget for cash tied up in stock: 'tribute to inexperience'; constant chase to pay suppliers' invoices
Relied on a USAID project for staff; when it stopped she paid salaries from savings and laid people off
Wanted a part-time business next to a baby; it needed full operations like a big system (100+ orders per delivery, 8+ items each)

Angry customer emails over fresh-produce quality and refunds
numbers: 100+ orders per weekly delivery, average over 8 items per order
August turnover equal to the first six months'

business: Zanateria (online marketplace for small Serbian makers)

Learned every step of the trade (production, installation, measuring) before managing

note: Forbes Srbija 'Opekao sam se u biznisu' (11 Aug 2024), several young entrepreneurs; only DaLux logged (the others are services, a distillery and education)

Trading since 2005

business: Market evidence: JYSK Albania (home-furnishing chain selling furniture, mattresses, duvets and pillows)
product: furniture, mattresses, duvets, pillows and home textiles
start_capital: not stated (franchise of a large Danish chain)

what_worked: of three product tiers (basic, plus, gold), the most expensive 'gold' tier sells better than the others (his words: 'surprisingly')
sells on price-to-quality and on guarantee and durability that 'you do not find in the neighbourhood market'
flat-packed products the customer carries home, cutting transport cost
what_failed: first store closed when the host mall ran into trouble, and no other site met the chain's standards
what hurts most is informal shops and markets selling poor-quality goods at the lowest prices
hard to find ~1,500 m2 sites outside Tirana; some products still seen as expensive in Albania

best sellers: furniture first, mattresses second, duvets and pillows third

business: FPM / Bestseller (furniture maker on the Tirana-Durrës highway)
product: furniture made in Albania, sold at home and exported to Italy and Romania

because it invoices properly, customers can pay in instalments or with a consumer loan for furniture, which favours it over informal makers
what_failed: as exports grew, home sales fell under fierce competition from unlicensed workshops that avoid costs and undercut prices; shops it supplied were undercut too
it had started to lose contact with Albanian customers while selling through traders

target 30% of sales at home and 70% export; 15-20% of turnover at home expected in 2019
